model_answer_outlines.question: Explain the transformer in two minutes.
model_answer_outlines.outline: Text becomes tokens, then embeddings plus positional information. Each layer applies self-attention (queries, keys, values; softmax of scaled query-key scores mixes the values), then a feed-forward network, with residual connections and layer norm. Decoder-only models add a causal mask and predict the next token; sampling rules such as temperature and top-p choose from the output distribution.

model_answer_outlines.question: RAG or fine-tuning?
model_answer_outlines.outline: RAG supplies knowledge (private, changing, large corpora, with citations and access control). Fine-tuning shapes behavior (format, tone, domain skill, cheaper smaller model). Start with prompting, add RAG for missing knowledge, fine-tune for consistent behavior or lower cost, combine when you need both, and decide with a measured eval set.

model_answer_outlines.question: How do you reduce hallucinations?
model_answer_outlines.outline: Ground answers with retrieval and require citations, allow I don't know, lower temperature for factual tasks, keep context short and relevant, verify claims against sources, validate structured output, route high-stakes cases to humans, and measure faithfulness on a golden set.

model_answer_outlines.question: How does LoRA work?
model_answer_outlines.outline: Freeze the weight matrix W and learn a low-rank update B times A with small rank r. This trains far fewer parameters, so it needs much less memory, and adapters are small enough to store and swap per task. QLoRA applies the same idea on a 4-bit quantized base model.

model_answer_outlines.question: How do you evaluate an LLM application?
model_answer_outlines.outline: Build a labeled eval set from real cases; use code checks first (format, exact match, tool-call correctness), then rubric-based judges calibrated against human labels and pairwise comparisons. Track quality, latency and cost together, run the suite in CI, and grow the set from production failures.

model_answer_outlines.question: Explain the KV cache.
model_answer_outlines.outline: Each new token needs the keys and values of all earlier tokens; storing them avoids recomputing them each step. It trades memory (growing with sequence length, batch, layers and heads) for speed. Grouped-query attention, quantized caches and paged allocation reduce the cost.

model_answer_outlines.question: A long document does not fit the context window. What do you do?
model_answer_outlines.outline: For question answering, chunk and retrieve. For summarization, use map-reduce or a rolling summary. If a large window is available, test whether stuffing the document works well enough, since details in the middle can be missed and cost rises. Always measure.

model_answer_outlines.question: Why is accuracy misleading?
model_answer_outlines.outline: On imbalanced data a model that always predicts the majority class scores high accuracy. Use precision, recall, F1, PR-AUC or a cost-weighted metric, and choose the threshold from the cost of each error type.

model_answer_outlines.question: What is prompt injection and how do you defend against it?
model_answer_outlines.outline: Untrusted text (from a user, retrieved content or a tool result) that the model treats as instructions. Defend in layers: least-privilege tools, separating trusted and untrusted content, output validation, approval for risky actions, sandboxing, monitoring and red-team tests. Assume the model can be fooled and limit the damage.

model_answer_outlines.question: Your RAG system gives wrong answers. Debug it.
model_answer_outlines.outline: Log one failing query end to end. If the right chunk was not retrieved, fix chunking, add hybrid search or query rewriting. If it was retrieved but ranked low, add a reranker. If it was in the context but the answer is wrong, tighten the prompt, reduce noise or test a stronger model. Fix one stage at a time and add the case to the eval set.
